response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.mktnote AS trading_pair, AVG(f.rebrate) AS avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) AS total_rebate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY (SUM(f.rebtotal) IS NULL) ASC, SUM(f.rebtotal) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A fee is 'high-rate' when feerate >= 0.0009. The cutoff value itself is counted as high-rate.
An inner join on exact text equality drops fees with no matching order. Fees with a NULL feerate are excluded by the filter.
AVG and SUM skip NULLs. A group where every rebtotal is NULL gets a NULL total, which sorts last. Ties in total rebate are left in arbitrary order.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rate means strictly above the cutoff (feerate > 0.0009), so fees exactly at 0.0009 are excluded.
